item.title: Mt. Ibuki: Wildflower Peak on the Shiga Border — Guide
item.description: Mount Ibuki, at 1,377 metres the highest mountain in Shiga, stands as a bold isolated massif on the Gifu border northeast of Lake Biwa, its limestone bulk catching the heaviest snows in western Japan — it holds a world record for snow depth. In the warm months its upper slopes become one of the country’s celebrated wildflower gardens, some 280 species carpeting the summit meadows through summer, while the panorama takes in Lake Biwa, the Suzuka range and the peaks of the Northern Alps.
